decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to hold the federal funds rate steady at 1/4 to 1/2 percent while noting that the case for an increase has strengthened.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth of economic activity has picked up from the modest pace seen in the first half of this year.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that economic growth has improved compared to earlier in the year.

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate is little changed in recent months, job gains have been solid, on average.
changes.explanation: This new addition highlights that hiring remains healthy even though the jobless rate has stayed steady.

changes.quote: Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced.
changes.explanation: The Fed feels the near-term threats to the economy are now more even, replacing the view that risks had diminished.

changes.quote: The Committee judges that the case for an increase in the federal funds rate has strengthened but decided, for the time being, to wait for further evidence of continued progress toward its objectives.
changes.explanation: Officials believe reasons to raise rates are growing stronger, but they chose to wait for more supporting data before acting.

changes.quote: Voting against the action were: Esther L. George, Loretta J. Mester, and Eric Rosengren, each of whom preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Three regional Fed presidents dissented and voted to raise rates immediately, showing a split within the committee.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee judges that the case for an increase in the federal funds rate has strengthened but decided, for the time being, to wait for further evidence of continued progress toward its objectives.
Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.16% APR costs about $50.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.66% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.44% would fall by about $5.00 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 254k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (August 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate hikes will be gradual and depend on upcoming economic data.
